description: Baseline: all built-in preset routes plus builtin-source sample under concurrency

asi.hypothesis: Establish broad route-level latency and reliability signal across the entire preset corpus before changing production code.
asi.observed: 124 requests completed without failures; p95 is 138.55 ms and mean is 79.897 ms. Reliability needs mutation/stress coverage because steady-state baseline did not reproduce intermittent failures.

description: Direct server-side disk lookup replaced SSR subrequest but regressed p95

asi.hypothesis: Removing the internal `/api/user-compositions` SSR fetch would reduce route overhead and remove a failure boundary.
asi.observed: Mean improved by 3.666 ms, but p95 regressed by 14.408 ms with no reliability difference in steady state.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed; direct filesystem module added complexity without a p95 win.
asi.next_action_hint: Improve benchmark stability and isolate normal versus builtin-source timing before revisiting the subrequest boundary.

description: Confirmation run of direct disk lookup showed repeat p95 regression

asi.hypothesis: The first direct-disk p95 regression might be benchmark noise because mean latency improved.
asi.observed: Second run again improved mean but regressed p95 more strongly, confirming filesystem completions create a worse latency tail under concurrency.
asi.rollback_reason: Repeated primary regression confirms this architecture is not suitable for the p95 target.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep SvelteKit internal fetch and optimize the absent-composition path or route observability instead.

description: Instrumented normal versus builtin-source p95 to localize route cost

asi.hypothesis: Splitting timings will show whether user-composition lookup dominates the preset route tail.
asi.observed: Normal-route p95 was 215.863 ms versus 67.575 ms for builtin-source requests, strongly localizing tail cost to user override lookup; overall variation also confirms a noisy benchmark.
asi.rollback_reason: No production improvement and the primary metric regressed; retain only autoresearch instrumentation.
asi.next_action_hint: Optimize the overwhelmingly common ENOENT path without replacing the internal fetch architecture.

description: Indexed User composition filenames to skip absent-override subrequests

asi.hypothesis: Most built-in routes have no User override, so a process-local filename index can skip nested HTTP and filesystem work while API writes keep the index coherent.
asi.observed: Overall p95 improved 14.3% from baseline and normal-route p95 fell to 120.023 ms with zero failures; builtin-source timing stayed effectively flat.
asi.correctness: Focused user-composition tests and full svelte-check passed. POST/PUT add index entries only after successful writes; DELETE removes after successful unlink.

description: Atomic User composition writes did not improve steady-state route score

asi.hypothesis: Temp-file plus atomic rename would prevent readers seeing partial JSON during autosave, eliminating a plausible intermittent load failure.
asi.observed: Correctness checks passed, but the steady-state route workload contains no concurrent writes and p95 regressed; this benchmark cannot validate the reliability benefit.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed and no measured failure was eliminated.
asi.next_action_hint: Use a dedicated concurrent read/write reliability phase before retrying atomic publication; idea recorded in .auto/ideas.md.

description: Direct disk loading only for indexed existing overrides was slower than retained route

asi.hypothesis: After the index removes ENOENT reads, directly loading only known-present overrides should avoid nested traced requests without the prior filesystem tail.
asi.observed: This beat the original baseline slightly but was 16.796 ms slower than the retained indexed-subrequest result; normal p95 worsened to 138.405 ms.
asi.rollback_reason: Regressed against the best retained implementation.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep SvelteKit fetch for present overrides; target response parsing or repeated loads instead of direct disk I/O.

description: Explicit Sentry capture for graceful preset load failures added observability but missed best p95

asi.hypothesis: Explicit captureException with bounded slug/source context would turn currently graceful 200 load failures into actionable Sentry issues without affecting success requests.
asi.observed: Checks passed and the design is optional-DSN safe, but the run was 11.217 ms slower than the retained best despite improving on original baseline.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed against the retained implementation.
asi.next_action_hint: Retry observability through the existing hooks/logger or confirm noise before retaining; success-path import cost may be avoidable with a helper already loaded server-side.

description: Eagerly started User composition index read at module evaluation

asi.hypothesis: Starting readdir during module evaluation would overlap index I/O with route module setup and reduce first-request latency.
asi.observed: The eager read did not beat the retained lazy shared promise; p95 was 16.517 ms slower than best.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regression; eager side effects also make module import behavior less explicit.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep lazy initialization and explore reducing work for known builtin slugs or caching present override responses.

description: Synchronous fast path after User composition index initialization regressed tail

asi.hypothesis: Returning synchronous Set membership after the first index load would avoid Promise/await microtasks on most absent-override routes.
asi.observed: The more complex boolean-or-Promise API regressed p95 sharply while barely affecting mean, so microtask overhead is not the bottleneck.
asi.rollback_reason: Large primary regression and less clear API contract.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not optimize Promise mechanics; focus on actual I/O/validation or benchmark repeated user override loads.

description: Repeated-load baseline across all preset routes

asi.hypothesis: A second complete pass better represents reload behavior and provides signal for safe response caching while preserving full-corpus coverage.
asi.observed: 223 requests completed with zero failures; repeated-load baseline p95 is 89.733 ms and normal-route p95 is 95.742 ms.

description: Five-second parsed User override cache regressed repeated-load score

asi.hypothesis: Caching recently validated User presets and synchronizing cache entries on API mutations would make repeated reloads faster without stale GUI saves.
asi.observed: First-pass cache population remained enough of the workload to worsen p95, and mean also regressed; cache bookkeeping did not pay for itself across two passes.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary and mean regression plus added cache-coherence complexity.
asi.next_action_hint: Avoid parsed route cache; investigate coalescing duplicate concurrent loads or endpoint validation cost.

description: Noise confirmation rerun of retained repeated-load baseline

asi.hypothesis: A no-change rerun will estimate benchmark variance before judging the final optimizations.
asi.observed: p95 varied from 89.733 to 120.14 ms with no code change while mean moved only 1.989 ms; tail is noisy under concurrent dev-server tracing.
asi.rollback_reason: No code change and no primary improvement.
asi.next_action_hint: Favor changes with large p95 wins and corroborating mean/normal-route gains; do not keep marginal tail changes.

description: Fallback to builtin preset when optional User override load fails

asi.hypothesis: A corrupt or transiently unreadable User override should not take down a valid built-in `/p/<slug>` route; logging the cause and falling back improves real reliability.
asi.observed: Correctness passed, but the no-fault workload cannot exercise the fallback and p95/mean both regressed versus baseline.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed and the reliability behavior lacks dedicated fault-injection proof.
asi.next_action_hint: Retry with injected override read/parse failures as part of a dedicated reliability workload; idea retained.

description: Final no-change confirmation of retained repeated-load behavior

asi.hypothesis: A final no-change rerun should show whether the repeated-load baseline is reproducible after the discarded fault-handling experiments.
asi.observed: p95 returned to within 0.823 ms of baseline with zero failures across 223 requests, confirming the large intermediate regressions were partly tail noise while mean remained stable.
asi.rollback_reason: No code change and no primary improvement.
asi.next_action_hint: Stop at the user-requested 15 total rounds; retained filename index is the only large, corroborated win.

description: Cached validated User-composition API wire responses for repeated route loads

asi.hypothesis: Caching only validated wire responses inside the existing User-composition API would accelerate repeated preset loads without adding cache checks to absent built-in routes; POST/PUT/DELETE kept entries coherent and a short TTL bounded manual-file staleness.
asi.observed: All 223 requests succeeded and checks passed, but p95 regressed 15.388 ms and mean regressed 2.126 ms versus the repeated-load baseline. Avoided second-pass file validation did not repay cache bookkeeping and first-pass cost.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric and mean both regressed; added cache coherence is not justified.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not cache API wire responses. The next reliability-focused attempt should use fault injection to measure atomic writes or builtin fallback directly rather than adding success-path caches.

description: Made the User-composition filename index fail open to authoritative API lookup

asi.hypothesis: Because the filename index is only an optimization, transient non-ENOENT readdir failures should return an unknown state and use the existing authoritative API path rather than causing every `/p/<slug>` load to fail.
asi.observed: All 223 routes succeeded; p95 improved slightly from 89.733 to 89.551 ms, normal-route p95 improved to 94.123 ms, and mean remained effectively flat. More importantly, the optimization no longer creates a new all-routes failure mode.
asi.correctness: Focused User-composition tests and full svelte-check passed. ENOENT still means an empty store, known absence still skips the API, and only unknown index state falls back to the pre-index API behavior.

description: Confirmation rerun of fail-open filename index after low-confidence keep

asi.hypothesis: A no-change confirmation run will determine whether the fail-open index change's tiny latency improvement was real or noise while checking that it remains performance-neutral and failure-free.
asi.observed: All 223 requests and correctness checks passed, but p95 rose to 106.025 ms and mean to 70.044 ms. This confirms the prior 0.2% speed improvement was noise; the retained value of eb314bb is reliability, not speed.
asi.rollback_reason: No new code change and no primary improvement; the previously committed fail-open behavior remains because this run only tested it.
asi.next_action_hint: Treat fail-open indexing as a reliability hardening with neutral/noisy performance. For another code experiment, use a dedicated fault-injection workload for atomic writes or built-in fallback rather than chasing sub-millisecond success-path changes.

description: Fault-stress baseline: concurrent valid autosaves exposed intermittent preset load failures

asi.hypothesis: A bounded disposable User-composition workload that overlaps valid PUT autosaves with GET route loads will reproduce the reported intermittent load failure without narrowing or weakening the full-corpus benchmark.
asi.observed: The broad corpus plus 32 stressed probe loads produced 26 semantic load failures, all returned as HTTP 200 error UI, while all 16 PUT operations and cleanup succeeded. This strongly supports partial/interleaved file visibility during concurrent writeFile calls as a real reliability cause.
asi.next_action_hint: Implement atomic temp-file publication with rename for POST/PUT and rerun the exact unchanged workload. Success means failures fall to zero without bypassing parsing, validation, or route behavior.
asi.benchmark_integrity: The workload still covers every preset route twice plus builtin-source samples; the disposable probe uses the same public APIs and a valid preset, and is always deleted.

description: Published User-composition writes atomically to prevent partial JSON reads

asi.hypothesis: Writing each valid User composition to a unique temporary file and atomically renaming it into place will ensure concurrent route readers observe either the previous complete JSON or the next complete JSON, never a partial/interleaved write.
asi.observed: Failures fell from 26 to 0 across the unchanged 255-request workload, including 32 route loads racing 16 valid autosaves. Load score improved from 260338.442 ms to 215.644 ms; p95 also fell from 338.442 to 215.644 ms and mean from 96.203 to 86.231 ms.
asi.correctness: Focused User-composition tests and full svelte-check passed. Temporary files use unique UUID names and are removed on write/rename failure; POST and PUT both use atomic publication.
asi.benchmark_integrity: The workload was unchanged from the fault-stress baseline and continued to validate every preset route twice plus builtin-source samples.

description: Confirmation rerun of atomic User-composition publication

asi.hypothesis: A no-change confirmation run will verify that atomic temp-file publication consistently eliminates concurrent autosave/read failures rather than benefiting from a lucky schedule.
asi.observed: The unchanged 255-request workload again produced zero route failures and zero write-operation failures. p95 improved further to 205.461 ms and mean to 84.218 ms; the original non-atomic baseline had 26 failures, 338.442 ms p95, and 96.203 ms mean.
asi.rollback_reason: No new source change was made in this confirmation iteration, so there is nothing new to retain or commit; atomic publication from 3a52eab remains retained.
asi.next_action_hint: The atomic-write result is now reproduced. A future code experiment should target write serialization/order semantics or fault-path Sentry issue capture, not re-test partial JSON visibility.

description: Serialized atomic User-composition writes per path to preserve request order under concurrent autosaves

asi.hypothesis: Serializing atomic writes per composition path would reduce concurrent filesystem contention and prevent an older autosave from publishing after a newer one, improving route-load p95 during the write/read stress phase.
asi.rollback_reason: Atomic publication already kept failures at zero, while per-path serialization regressed load_score_ms from the retained 215.64 ms best to 228.477 ms and added queue complexity.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep independent atomic writes. Pursue fault-path Sentry observability only with dedicated fault injection, or improve the broad route p95 outside persistence writes rather than serializing autosaves.
asi.finding: Write serialization improves ordering semantics but provides no reliability gain in this workload and worsens the measured route tail.

description: Fault-injection baseline: corrupt optional User override breaks its valid built-in route

asi.hypothesis: A dedicated corrupt-override probe will reproduce the remaining reliability gap: an unreadable optional User composition currently makes an otherwise valid built-in Preset route show load-error UI.
asi.rollback_reason: Baseline intentionally reproduced one semantic route failure and made no production improvement; retain only the autoresearch fault-injection workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Catch User override load/parse failures for slugs with a valid built-in Preset, emit bounded actionable server logging, and fall back to that built-in. Preserve load-error behavior for user-only slugs.
asi.finding: A truncated User override returned HTTP 200 but rendered the route load-error UI, adding the expected 10,000 ms semantic-failure penalty. The API setup and cleanup both succeeded.

description: Fallback to built-in Preset when an optional User override is corrupt or unreadable

asi.hypothesis: If an optional User override cannot be read or parsed, logging the bounded failure and falling back to an existing built-in Preset will keep the route usable while preserving errors for user-only slugs.
asi.rollback_reason: The fault probe improved from one semantic failure to zero, but correctness checks could not start because node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs is missing. A checks_failed result cannot be retained.
asi.next_action_hint: Repair the local pnpm/node_modules links without changing application behavior, then rerun the same fallback implementation and unchanged fault-injection workload.
asi.finding: The production behavior eliminated the injected corrupt-override failure, but validation infrastructure is currently broken independently of the code change.

description: Retried corrupt-override fallback after repairing package links

asi.hypothesis: After repairing the stale top-level Vitest link, the built-in fallback should eliminate the injected corrupt-override failure and pass correctness checks.
asi.rollback_reason: The behavior again eliminated all failures and reached 214.657 ms, but pnpm's failed offline sharp install did not recreate node_modules/.bin/vitest, so checks still could not start.
asi.next_action_hint: Repair node_modules/.bin command links (or complete a script-ignored offline install), verify pnpm exec vitest starts, then rerun the identical fallback and workload.
asi.finding: Fallback performance and reliability are reproducible, but this run remains unretainable solely because the package-manager command shim is missing.

description: Fallback to built-in Preset when an optional User override is corrupt or unreadable

asi.hypothesis: When an optional User override cannot be read or parsed, logging the bounded failure and falling back to an existing built-in Preset will eliminate the reproduced semantic route failure while preserving errors for user-only slugs.
asi.finding: The unchanged fault-injection workload improved from one semantic failure and a 10,297.812 ms score to zero failures and 252.692 ms. Focused route tests verify built-in fallback, user precedence, source=builtin bypass, missing routes, and continued error behavior for user-only slugs.
asi.validation: Benchmark and full autoresearch checks passed after repairing local pnpm command links.
asi.next_action_hint: Confirm the retained fallback once under the unchanged fault workload, then target actionable structured Sentry context for this graceful recovery without adding success-path imports.

description: Confirmation run of retained corrupt-override built-in fallback

asi.hypothesis: A no-change confirmation under the unchanged corrupt-override workload will verify that the retained built-in fallback consistently eliminates semantic route failures and remains performance-neutral.
asi.rollback_reason: No source change was made in this confirmation iteration, so there is nothing new to retain; commit fe7de7a remains the retained implementation.
asi.next_action_hint: The fallback is reproduced with zero failures. Next target actionable structured Sentry context for graceful fallback without introducing a success-path import, or stop if observability cannot be measured without distorting the workload.
asi.finding: The second checks-passing run again produced zero failures, with 242.333 ms load score versus 252.692 ms in the retained run. Full checks passed.

description: Lazy explicit Sentry issue capture for corrupt-override fallback

asi.hypothesis: Dynamically importing Sentry only on the corrupt-override recovery path would create an actionable exception issue with bounded route tags while leaving normal route loads unaffected.
asi.rollback_reason: Failures remained at zero, but load_score_ms regressed from the retained 252.692 ms run and 242.333 ms confirmation to 285.584 ms. Explicit capture is not justified by the primary metric.
asi.next_action_hint: Rely on the existing server consoleLoggingIntegration for the bounded fallback log, or add structured context centrally in hooks.server.ts only if a dedicated observability assertion can prove value without adding route-path latency.
asi.finding: Even fault-only awaited Sentry loading correlated with a broader p95 and mean regression; avoid route-local SDK imports.

description: Coalesced concurrent GET reads for the same User composition

asi.hypothesis: Sharing only simultaneously in-flight reads and validation for the same User-composition slug will reduce filesystem and schema-validation contention during concurrent autosave reloads without caching responses beyond request completion.
asi.finding: The unchanged workload remained failure-free and improved load_score_ms from the retained 252.692 ms to 238.771 ms; mean also improved from 87.515 ms to 86.758 ms. A focused test proves same-slug requests share one read while the in-flight entry is removed after completion.
asi.validation: Benchmark and full autoresearch checks passed.
asi.next_action_hint: Run a no-change confirmation because the p95 improvement over the immediately preceding 242.333 ms confirmation is modest. Retain only if failure-free behavior and tail latency reproduce.

description: Confirmation run of in-flight User-composition read coalescing

asi.hypothesis: A no-change confirmation will determine whether the modest tail improvement from same-slug in-flight read coalescing is reproducible.
asi.rollback_reason: No source change was made, and the confirmation regressed from 238.771 ms to 265.360 ms with a worse mean. The retained coalescing result is not performance-confirmed.
asi.next_action_hint: Run an explicit removal experiment for in-flight coalescing under the unchanged workload. If removal matches or beats this result, drop the added concurrency complexity; otherwise treat performance as noisy and judge it only on concurrency semantics.
asi.finding: Failures remained zero, but the p95 improvement did not reproduce.

description: Removed in-flight User-composition read coalescing to test whether complexity was justified

asi.hypothesis: If the coalescing win was benchmark noise, removing it should match or improve the unchanged workload while simplifying request semantics.
asi.rollback_reason: Removal regressed load_score_ms to 272.108 ms, worse than both the retained 238.771 ms result and its 265.360 ms confirmation, with no mean improvement. Keep coalescing.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain bounded in-flight coalescing. For the remaining rounds, avoid more persistence micro-optimizations; use no-change stability runs or stop after the configured round limit.
asi.finding: Neither direction produced a large stable p95 separation, but removal offered no performance or reliability benefit and discarded a legitimate reduction in duplicate concurrent work.

description: No-change stability run of retained fallback and in-flight read coalescing

asi.hypothesis: A further no-change run will characterize noise after the removal experiment and verify that the retained fallback plus bounded coalescing remains failure-free.
asi.rollback_reason: No source change was made, so there is nothing new to retain or commit; retained commits fe7de7a and 1ffcab2 remain unchanged.
asi.next_action_hint: One configured round remains. Use a final no-change run to close with reliability evidence rather than adding another low-confidence micro-optimization.
asi.finding: The workload again produced zero failures, with 223.933 ms p95 and improved mean, confirming that recent p95 movement is largely environmental while reliability remains stable.

description: Final no-change reliability confirmation for preset routes under autosave and corrupt-override stress

asi.hypothesis: A final unchanged run will close the configured experiment budget with evidence that atomic publication, corrupt-override fallback, and bounded in-flight reads remain failure-free across the full preset corpus.
asi.rollback_reason: No source change was made in this confirmation iteration, so there is nothing new to retain; the retained implementation remains in commits 3a52eab, fe7de7a, and 1ffcab2.
asi.next_action_hint: Stop the autoresearch loop at the configured 15-round segment limit. Review and integrate the retained commits; do not add more benchmark-driven micro-optimizations.
asi.finding: Final workload completed with zero route or operation failures, 213.704 ms p95, and 82.727 ms mean. Full checks passed.
